name: Devotional
description: Short scripture-anchored reflections — a verse, a thought, a takeaway. Distinct from raw prayer in that the listener is being TAUGHT something rooted in a passage, not just praying through it. Best for channels that want a steady daily-devotion cadence ('today's verse', 'a thought from Psalm 23'). Pair with calm nature / candle / sunrise B-Roll.
tagline: A verse. A thought. A breath.
exampleTopics: What the Beatitudes Teach Us About Quiet Strength
Trusting When You Can't See the Path
audienceHint: Christians who want a 3-7 minute scripture-grounded reflection alongside their morning coffee or before bed.
scriptContext: Anchor every devotional in ONE specific passage. Open with the verse spoken aloud, unpack it in 2-3 short reflections, end with a single takeaway the listener can carry through the day. Avoid theological tangents; stay practical and pastoral.
titleShapeRules: Titles MUST anchor on a SPECIFIC scripture passage OR a SPECIFIC pastoral topic. Direct and teaching-oriented — never poetic.
Use ONE of these established shapes (vary the passage / topic across the batch):
- 'A Thought on {Book Chapter:Verse}'         (e.g. 'A Thought on Psalm 23', 'A Thought on John 14:27')
- 'Why {Book Chapter:Verse} Still Matters'     (e.g. 'Why Joshua 1:9 Still Matters')
- '{N} Lessons from {Book Chapter:Verse}'      (e.g. 'Three Lessons from Proverbs 3:5-6')
- 'What {Book / Figure} Teaches Us About X'    (e.g. 'What the Beatitudes Teach Us About Quiet Strength', 'What Job Knew About Suffering')
- 'Lessons from {Parable / Figure}'            (e.g. 'Lessons from the Prodigal Son')
- 'A Devotion on X'                            (e.g. 'A Devotion on Anxiety', 'A Devotion for Tired Mothers')
- 'Trusting When X'                            (e.g. 'Trusting When You Can't See the Path')
- Nature/scenery modifiers ('at Sunset's Edge', 'in the Garden', 'Moonlit Waters')
- Atmospheric adjectives ('A Quiet Devotion', 'A Gentle Thought', 'A Reflective…') — keep it instructional, not poetic
- Vague abstractions ('Inner Peace', 'Sacred Moments') without a SPECIFIC passage / topic anchor
REQUIRED: every title points at a concrete scripture reference OR a concrete pastoral teaching subject. The audience comes here to LEARN something from a passage, not to enjoy poetry.
